chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، الْأَشْلُ، كُوفِيٌّ، مَوْلًى. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ.

translations.en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim ibn Abd al-Rahman, al-Ashl, Kufan, a client. He narrated from Abu Basir.

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ. وَأَبُوهُ ثِقَةٌ، رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَر، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Weak. His father was thiqa, he narrated from Abu Ja'far, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* highlights the nuanced methodology of Shia hadith criticism by contrasting the weak status of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim al-Ashl with the reliability of his father, illustrating the importance of familial scholarly lineage in assessing narrators. While ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is deemed *ḍaʿīf* (weak) in his transmission from Abū Baṣīr, his father’s trustworthiness and direct narration from the Imams Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh underscore the value of preserving authentic chains through reliable family lines.
en.seo_question: Who is Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim al-Ashl and what is his status in hadith sciences?
